# windows_certificate (Resource)

Manages a single X.509 certificate in a Windows certificate store (`Cert:\<location>\<store>`) on a remote Windows host via SSH and PowerShell (`X509Certificate2` / `X509Certificate2Collection` + `X509Store.Add`).

Exactly one payload must be set: `certificate_pem` (a PEM-encoded certificate, stored in state in normalised form) or `pfx_base64_wo` (a base64-encoded PFX/PKCS#12 bundle, WriteOnly, never in state) together with `pfx_wo_version`. The payload and the optional `pfx_password_wo` travel to the host on stdin and never appear in the script, logs or state.

Rotation of a PFX bundle is driven exclusively by `pfx_wo_version`: bump the version and re-apply with the new bundle (its value cannot be diffed). Changing only the bundle without bumping the version is a no-op. Changing any identity attribute replaces the certificate: use a `lifecycle` `create_before_destroy` block when the new certificate must be usable before the old one is removed.

Only `friendly_name` is updated in place. `delete_private_key` (default `true`) controls whether destroy also deletes the private key from the key store.

Import format: `<store_location>/<store_name>/<thumbprint>` (e.g. `LocalMachine/My/A1B2...`). A PFX-backed certificate is recognised by its private key and imports with `pfx_wo_version = 1`: add the bundle and password back in configuration before the next apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    windows = {
      source  = "kfrlabs/windows"
      version = "~> 0.1"
    }
  }
}

provider "windows" {
  host     = var.windows_host
  username = var.windows_username
  password = var.windows_password
}

# Import a public certificate from PEM. Only the first CERTIFICATE block is
# imported; the value is stored in state in normalised form.
resource "windows_certificate" "web" {
  certificate_pem = file("${path.module}/web.crt")
  friendly_name   = "tf-web"

  # Bound every remote operation explicitly. Without this block each operation
  # defaults to 10 minutes; a stalled PowerShell/SSH session then surfaces a
  # timeout diagnostic instead of blocking Terraform indefinitely.
  timeouts = {
    create = "10m"
    read   = "5m"
    update = "10m"
    delete = "10m"
  }

  # Replacing a certificate removes the old thumbprint and adds the new one.
  # Create the replacement first so the store always holds a usable
  # certificate during rotation.
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

# Import a PFX bundle with an exportable private key. The bundle and password
# are WriteOnly: they never reach state or logs. Rotation is driven by
# pfx_wo_version: bump it and re-apply with the new bundle.
# Note: terraform import always records exportable = false in state. After
# importing a PFX-backed certificate, set exportable in configuration to match
# the host before the first apply (exportable forces replacement when it
# differs).
resource "windows_certificate" "web_pfx" {
  pfx_base64_wo   = filebase64("${path.module}/web.pfx")
  pfx_password_wo = var.pfx_password
  pfx_wo_version  = 1
  exportable      = true
  friendly_name   = "tf-web-pfx"

  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}

output "web_thumbprint" {
  value       = windows_certificate.web.thumbprint
  description = "SHA-1 thumbprint of the imported certificate."
}
```

## Schema

### Optional

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `certificate_pem` (String) PEM-encoded certificate (the CERTIFICATE block; surrounding text such as a chain or private key is ignored, only the first certificate is imported). Exactly one of `certificate_pem` and `pfx_base64_wo` must be set. Stored in state in normalised form. Changing it replaces the certificate.
- `delete_private_key` (Boolean) Whether destroy also deletes the private key from the key store. Defaults to `true`. Only affects destroy.
- `exportable` (Boolean) Marks the imported private key exportable. PFX bundles only; rejected with `certificate_pem`. Immutable after creation (ForceNew). Defaults to `false`.
- `friendly_name` (String) Display name of the certificate. The only attribute updated in place; setting it to `""` clears the display name.
- `pfx_base64_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only base64-encoded PFX/PKCS#12 bundle (TPF v1.14+ WriteOnly). Exactly one of `certificate_pem` and `pfx_base64_wo` must be set. The plaintext is never persisted in state; rotation is driven exclusively by `pfx_wo_version`. Changing only the bundle without bumping the version is a no-op.
- `pfx_password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) Write-only password decrypting the PFX bundle (TPF v1.14+ WriteOnly). Omit for an unprotected bundle. The value must not contain carriage return or line feed characters (rejected at plan time): secrets are read with `ReadLine()`, so anything from the first line break on would be silently truncated. If the value comes from `file()`, wrap it with `trimspace()` to strip the trailing newline.
- `pfx_wo_version` (Number) Version counter for `pfx_base64_wo` rotation. Change this value to replace the certificate with a new bundle: when it changes, the provider re-imports the configured bundle. Conventionally starts at 1. Changing only the bundle without changing this version leaves the stored certificate untouched.
- `store_location` (String) Certificate store location: `LocalMachine` (default) or `CurrentUser`. Immutable after creation (ForceNew).
- `store_name` (String) Certificate store name (e.g. `My`, the default). Immutable after creation (ForceNew). Must not contain `/` or `\`.
- `timeouts` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `dns_names` (List of String) DNS entries of the subject-alternative-name extension, as observed on the host (possibly empty).
- `has_private_key` (Boolean) Whether the stored certificate carries a private key, as observed on the host.
- `id` (String) Resource identifier: `<store_location>/<store_name>/<thumbprint>`.
- `issuer` (String) Distinguished name of the issuer, as observed on the host.
- `not_after` (String) End of the validity period (RFC 3339 UTC), as observed on the host.
- `not_before` (String) Start of the validity period (RFC 3339 UTC), as observed on the host.
- `serial_number` (String) Serial number hex string, as observed on the host.
- `subject` (String) Distinguished name of the subject, as observed on the host.
- `thumbprint` (String) SHA-1 thumbprint (uppercase hex), as observed on the host.
- `thumbprint_sha256` (String) SHA-256 digest of the certificate (uppercase hex), as observed on the host.

<a id="nestedatt--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).
- `delete` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Setting a timeout for a Delete operation is only applicable if changes are saved into state before the destroy operation occurs.
- `read` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours). Read operations occur during any refresh or planning operation when refresh is enabled.
- `update` (String) A string that can be [parsed as a duration](https://pkg.go.dev/time#ParseDuration) consisting of numbers and unit suffixes, such as "30s" or "2h45m". Valid time units are "s" (seconds), "m" (minutes), "h" (hours).

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import an existing certificate by <store_location>/<store_name>/<thumbprint>.
# A certificate carrying a private key is assumed PFX-backed and imports with
# pfx_wo_version = 1: add the bundle and password back in configuration before
# the next apply. A keyless certificate imports with its normalised PEM in
# certificate_pem.
# Note: import always sets exportable = false in state. If the private key was
# imported as exportable, set exportable = true in configuration before the
# first apply so the plan matches the host (exportable forces replacement).
terraform import windows_certificate.web "LocalMachine/My/A1B2C3D4E5F60718293A4B5C6D7E8F9012345678"
```
